subject: PlaneGeometry
question: The diagram shows a spiral of isosceles triangles. The largest angle in each triangle is $100^{\circ}$. The grey triangle is number 0. Each subsequent triangle (numbered 1, 2, 3, ...) joins the previous one along an edge, as shown. Triangle 3 only partially covers triangle 0. What is the number of the first triangle that exactly covers triangle 0? <image1>
original_question: The diagram shows a spiral of isosceles triangles. The largest angle in each of the triangles is $100^{\circ}$. The grey triangle is number 0 . Each of the following triangles (numbered 1, 2, 3, ...) join by one edge to the previous one, as shown. As you can see triangle 3 only partially covers triangle 0. What is the number of the first triangle that exactly covers triangle 0 ? <image1>
